Hairy cell leukemia (HCL) is a rare, indolent B-cell neoplasm accounting for less than 2% of all leukemias. It is characterized by the presence of mature lymphocytes with typical hairy projections within the peripheral blood, bone marrow, and spleen, resulting in pancytopenia and splenomegaly. Purine analogs such as cladribine and pentostatin have been the mainstay of treatment for HCL. Despite high responsiveness to first-line therapy with purine analogs, almost half of the patients with HCL relapse and become progressively resistant to these medications.
